title: Composition with a continuous map
rationale: Continuity on all of R does not imply uniform continuity (f(x) = x^2 is the standard witness), so the proof's bridging step is wrong as written; the correct proof restricts to a compact set of probability close to one using the a.s. finiteness of X. The statement itself is the continuous mapping theorem and is true, so the audit-correct statement judgment is not_established from this proof: refuting it fabricates a counterexample, and establishing it supplies an argument the authors did not write.
note: A passing response must flag the uniform-continuity step on lines 12-14 and must NOT report the statement as refuted or established.
